Adds slack deployment messages to the buildkite pipeline. It might be better to have them in the deploy tool, but this can be a first step.

author: emiltin
body:
Splits Probe into Listener and subclass Collector, and rename ProbeCollection to Notifier. Notifier is now a module.
 
Message capturing has been moved out of Archive and into Collector. The collector inserts inself into a Notifier, and once it has collected what it wants, if removes itself againg.

When creating a supervisor, you can pass a new options for collecting initial message. If can be used to collect messages exchanged when starting up connections, which is useful when testing.

Limits storage of messeges in Archive to 100, to avoid growing memory usa in long-running processes.

Moves proxy wait methods to a module.

author: sponglord
body:
<!-- 🎉 Thank you for submitting a pull request! 🎉  -->

## Summary
A merchant wants to know when a shopper is entering their merchant-branded card into in a card component that is not configured for it - and specifically what brands are supported and what type of card is being entered.
This boils down to exposing the `supportedBrands` and `detectedBrands` from the `/binLookup` API.
So there is now a possibility for the merchant to add a new callback `onBinLookup` which will receive an object that looks like this:
```
{
  type: 'card', // could be specific brand if component is dedicated to a single brand e.g. 'bcmc'
  detectedBrands: ["mc"],
  supportedBrands: ["visa", "amex", ]
}
```

## Tested scenarios
`onBinLookup` is called if defined by the merchant. If not defined there is a default set which catches the callback and prevents an error being thrown


**Fixed issue**:  COWEB-889

author: aherrmann-da
body:
Closes #7957

Makes the OAuth2 requests emitted by the auth middleware configurable using Jsonnet templates.

- This requires additional state in the auth middleware's request handlers. To avoid long argument lists this factors out the handlers into a class.
- This uses [databricks/sjsonnet](https://github.com/databricks/sjsonnet) for parsing and interpreting of Jsonnet. The necessary setup and interpret steps are extracted from the [sjsonnet main](https://github.com/databricks/sjsonnet/blob/ed355288040017a0e441f308188f35ccacba34fb/sjsonnet/server/src/sjsonnet/SjsonnetServerMain.scala).
- Users can pass custom templates for auth, token, and refresh requests through command-line flags.
- The builtin request formats are also expressed as templates that are bundled as JAR resources.
- This adds a test-suite for the template handling code.

author: athei
body:
Contracts which are no longer able to pay their rent need to be removed from the chain in order to reclaim the space they occupy. In order to do so a `claim_surcharge` dispatchable can be submitted which in case of success rewards some newly minted balance to the sender (`SurchargeReward`).

Depending on the value of `SurchargeReward` and the current weight price it is possible that a situation may arise where the costs of creating a minimal contract is lower than the `SurchargeReward` gained when removing this contract. This would incentivise to create contracts for the sole reason to remove them and make a profit.

This PR  thwarts this unwanted behaviour by recording the rent a contract payed over its lifetime and cap the `SurchargeReward` by this amount.

Additionally, we make any successful call of `claim_surcharge` free for the sender. This is a service to the network and we want to incentivize calling this to remove stale contracts.

body:
<!-- Type of change
Please label this PR with one of the existing labels, depending on the scope of your change
-->

## What does this PR do?

It uses the new built-in `filebeat` step from the APM Pipeline Library (see elastic/apm-pipeline-library#887), which runs filebeat configured to capture all docker logs, storing them in a well-known place for Jenkins to archive those logs in its UI.

Before these changes, we were outputting certain container logs to STDOUT (metricbeat container in the metricbeat test suite, and elastic-agent in the fleet one), and here we are enabling that only for development mode, which means setting the environment variable `DEVELOPER_MODE=true`.

In that process, we refactored the helper method to read boolean env vars, removing the `error` output parameter: we weree not using them at all, so let's apply KISS.

Finally, for metricbeat, we are not failing the step if the logs are not available, we are going to simply print a warning instead.

<!-- Mandatory
Explain here the changes you made on the PR. Please explain the WHAT: patterns used, algorithms implemented, design architecture, etc.
-->

## Why is it important?

Because the containers are controlled by the test runner (godog's Before/After suite/scenario test life cycle hooks), they are killed right after the tests finish. For that reason we were not able to store the logs or the containers in place using the existing built-in steps from the APM pipeline library, such as `dockerLogs` (see https://github.com/elastic/apm-pipeline-library/blob/master/vars/dockerLogs.groovy).

With this new approach, filebeat will be started and in a closure it will run the tests, so filebeat will capture all Docker container logs during the execution.

<!-- Mandatory
Explain here the WHY, or the rationale/motivation for the changes.
-->

- [x] Because we are using the closure, the filebeat.start method is called before the tests.

## How to test this PR locally

The main functionality resides in Jenkins, so it's not testable locally.

For the refactors in this PR, running the tests in `DEVELOPER_MODE="false"` (or not set) will not print metricbeat/elastic-agent logs in STDOUT, even though the LOG_LEVEL is set to TRACE (the lowest, showing the most). 

```shell
# elastic-agent
SUITE="fleet" TAGS="fleet_mode_agent && unenroll" TIMEOUT_FACTOR=3 LOG_LEVEL=TRACE make -C e2e functional-test
# metricbeat
SUITE="metricbeat" TAGS="metricbeat" TIMEOUT_FACTOR=3 LOG_LEVEL=TRACE make -C e2e functional-test
```

n the future even in case of wrap-arounds.
* Use an authoritative citation for SipHash-2-4

Comments from Benjamin Kaduk
* Fix timing inconsistency of section 4.3 and section 5
* Motivate the use of SipHash-2-4 as pseudorandom function
* Consolidate everything after the first paragraph in the Abstract into a single second paragraph
* Single implementation no anycast services also benefit for a well-studies algorithm
* Avoid the word 'nonce' with Client Cookies
* Language style improvements in "tracking of Client Cookies prevention" description
* Make the single server case more explicit in Server Cookie construction description
* A DNS Server MAY generate a new Server Cookie more often than every half hour
* Length verifications of Server Cookies so byte string input into SipHash-2-4 is injective and not suscep
tible to data substitution attacks.
* Explain how different Client Cookie for each server provides minimal authentication (in Section 3)
* Provide Security Considerations for Server Cookies
* Mention Timestamp values in test vector examples
* Miscellaneous other minor editorial suggestions

Comments from Erik Kline
* Section 1: s/in a Client protecting fashion/in a privacy protecting fashion/

body:
Bumps [semantic-release](https://github.com/semantic-release/semantic-release) from 17.0.4 to 17.3.1. **This update includes a security fix.**
Vulnerabilities fixed

Sourced from The GitHub Security Advisory Database.

Secret disclosure when containing characters that become URI encoded

Impact

Secrets that would normally be masked by semantic-release can be accidentally disclosed if they contain characters that become encoded when included in a URL.

Patches

Fixed in v17.2.3

Workarounds

Secrets that do not contain characters that become encoded when included in a URL are already masked properly.

Affected versions: <= 17.2.2

@jameskleeh what do you think?

author: hristostaykov
body:
…ersistent.

During recover we recover either in an Active View, or the first Inactive View we have reached.
In other words in the cases we have multiple View Changes we can reach inconsistent Complaint/View scenario.
An example is as follows:

1. We have a setup of Replicas with F=3 and all are up and executing Client requests in view 0, thus view 0 is Active.
2. We crash Replica 0, 1 and 2.
3. View Change is initiated and happens multiple times, because now the next 2 expected Primaries (1 and 2)
   are also down and no View gets activated during this process.
4. We chose a Replica, for example Replica 6 and restart it right before it manages to activate View 3,
   the View that the View Change process will reach, because Replicas 1 and 2 are down.
5. After the restart, Replica 6 will recover in View 1.

The described scenario does not allow us to persist the Complaints (ReplicaAsksToLeaveViewMsg-s) because we might
reach a situation after restarting a Replica where it is in a lower View than the last stored Complaint it has generated.

We have a solution though which does not involve persistent Storage.
Currently the Replicas reject ReplicaAsksToLeaveViewMsg that has been generated from itself,
even if it is properly signed. This was the initial cause for the necessity of persistence.
If we accept Complaints generated from ourself that carry the correct signature we do not have
to persist them. Once a Replica is restarted and recovers in a lower View than it was previously
it will catch up by receiving View Change messages from peers and if it has generated a ReplicaAsksToLeaveViewMsg
for this higher View, the peers will have stored it (in RAM) and send it to the restarted Replica.

Final note: Complaints (with the proper signatures) backing up a ViewChangeMsg will be persisted inside the ViewChangeMsg itself.

Bumps [webpack](https://github.com/webpack/webpack) from 4.41.5 to 4.46.0.
Release notes

Sourced from webpack's releases.

v4.45.0

Features

  • resolve server-relative requests relative to project context by default

Bugfixes

  • fix a bug where splitChunk minSize is not handled correctly
  • fix a bug where the order of splitChunk cacheGroups is not handled correctly

v4.44.2

Bugfixes

  • make sure to generate correct chunk connection for blocks that are only connected in some runtimes
    • fixes a bug where filename contains undefined hash at runtime

v4.44.1

Bugfixes

  • fix bug in sideEffects optimization when using export * from "non-esm" and a default export.
  • add missing optional peerDependencies for webpack-cli and webpack-command to support Yarn 2

v4.44.0

Features

  • Improve sideEffects flag behavior when dynamic modules are part of the tree
    • Fixes a bug which causes empty modules (or type-only modules) to "break" Tree Shaking
  • add splitChunks.enforceSizeThreshold to allow enfore splitting larger chunks unrelated from other limiations
    • Not set by default to avoid breaking change
    • It will be set by default to 50k in webpack 5
    • It's recommended to set it in webpack 4 too
  • add support for resolve.roots and default resolve.roots: [context]
    • This allows to resolve server-relative urls (e.g. /src/abc) to the project root (or other locations when configured)
    • This allows to use loaders that rely on that behavior

Bugfixes

  • fix bug where splitChunks produced non-optimal results when minSize is set to 0
    • This lead to NaNs in some places which breaks ordering
  • Fix bug which lead to HMR not working for splitChunks in entrypoints
  • force update watchpack and chokidar for chokidar bugfix which causes files to stop being watched

**Motivation**

**Summary**

One breaking change to the smart contracts that I made is to add a param to the `PriceProposed` event: `expirationTimestamp`. Without this param, the OO client would need to query the block timestamp of the `PriceProposed` event and then compute its expiration time, which may require an additional web3 call. Do you think this is a reasonable addition to the contracts?

This should be the last OO client PR before we start implementing the OO keeper which takes the OO client state and determines how to respond to `unproposedRequests` and `undisputedProposals`, for example.

Open questions:
- Should the OO client make additional DVM web3 calls to determine which disputed price requests can be resolved?
- Will the OO keeper settle proposals?

author: texpert
body:
### What problem is the code solving?
Adding a new endpoint for Flow to validate if the product has enough stock available during the checkout.

### How does this change address the problem?
By adding a new controller to handle non related webhooks requests from Flow. 

### Why is this the best solution?
This looked like the simplest solution. Let me share some notes I wrote while working on this.
* Adding a new controller instead of using the current one for webhooks, looks a little better in order to avoid mixing them and generating possible confusions in the future.
* Reusing `Spree::Variant#available_online` method to calculate if there is enough online stock for certain Item.
* There is no specific authentication method associated to this new endpoint since this information is public and I don't think there is any need to have an authentication here.

### Share the knowledge
Unfortunately there are no automated tests cases for this ticket yet. since in order to configure them we will need lots of files from mejuri-web repository into the dummy app and that might create some maintenance issues in the future. Probably a better to test this would be to configure a locust or a feature test to handle the testing?

body:
The internal representation of a TimePeriod is an unsigned 32 bit integer counting milliseconds.

The maximum value 4294967295 is used to encode the special value 'never', thus the maximum usable value for a TimePeriod is 4294967294 milliseconds or a little more than one month, 19 days and six and a half hours.

Without this change, code is generated that leads to an integer overflow for too large TimePeriods. The compiler would warn, but this verification makes sure that the values are within bounds before the code is generated and compiled.

    src/main.cpp: In function 'void setup()':
    src/main.cpp:1005:53: warning: large integer implicitly truncated to unsigned type [-Woverflow]
       ota_otacomponent->start_safe_mode(5, 4294967295ULL);

## Checklist:
  - [X] The code change is tested and works locally.
  - ~~Tests have been added to verify that the new code works (under `tests/` folder).~~
  - The effectiveness has been proven by setting the `boot_timeout` for the `ota` component in `tests/test1.yaml` to `4294967295ms` which makes the test fail as expected. Any other TimerPeriod parameter would be checked exatly the same way.

author: brandonkelly
body: ### Description This PR adds a new “Allowed URL Types” setting to URL fields, with “Web page”, “Telephone”, and “Email” options: When 2+ options are checked, a dropdown will be displayed to the left of the URL input, which lists the options you’ve selected. Phone numbers will get a `tel:` prefix added; emails will get a `mailto:` prefix. But those will be hidden from the actual UI. I also ended up removing the Placeholder setting, because we would have needed to add URL type-specific placeholder settings, which is the wrong direction we should be going (#7303). ### Related issues #5497

body:
### Status
PENDING REVIEW

### What does this PR accomplish?
- Restructures the way whitelabel tests are organized
- Makes all tests run in isolation (as part of #14339)
- Cuts down the tests running time by a third - from around 95s to 60-65s on average
- Introduces some of the Cypress official best practices
- Makes it easier to read:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/31325167/104248294-84b9cb00-5469-11eb-9648-0a81dee8c638.png)
vs.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/31325167/104247898-ddd52f00-5468-11eb-95b7-904a17360628.png)


### Additional context
For some unknown reason, I managed to include two other commits in this PR.
- Run all tests in isolation for `drill_through.cy.spec.js` (https://github.com/metabase/metabase/pull/14346/commits/827b5939821b9b84a0948204cf783ef178bb479e) and
- Run all tests in isolation for `snippet-permissions.cy.spec.js` (https://github.com/metabase/metabase/pull/14346/commits/5fa8d998eba0bc5967eb059a5007200c0d79105c)

However, they don't have any significant code changes so I'll leave them here. The simple CI check should confirm that they are working as intended.

author: tim-evans
body:
Our editors are requesting to identify blocks of content and mark them with fragment identifiers so they can directly link to them. This is used often for tables of contents to jump to specific sections of a page, or for FAQs, for example.  You can see an example of this on The New Yorker's [FAQ page](https://www.newyorker.com/about/faq).

By adding this as an annotation attribute instead of an annotation, we'll be able to collect more robust information about what _kinds_ of content our editors are linking to and it'll be easier to implement a minimal solution in renderers for this that are appropriate (most renderers that use DOM will need to add an `id` attribute to the block element).

I've added here a couple of changes:
1. Added `class` and `id` to `GlobalAttributes` so we can correctly type check against HTML annotations
2. Added `anchorName` to `Blockquote`, `Group`, `Heading`, `IframeEmbed`, `Image`, `ListItem`, `Paragraph`, `Pullquote`, `Sidebar`, and `VideoEmbed`. (List item is included but not list because linking to a list item I think is way more specific, although I could see cases to be made to link to lists. If anyone feels that List should have this as well, lmk!)
3. Added rendering to the HTML renderer to render all `anchorName`s as `id`s on these elements
4. Added conversion rules to turn `id`s on HTML elements into `anchorName`s.

## EventData
- handle metadata HashMap in the constructor.  The caller already knows what the content will be when using ```EventData::json``` or ```EventData::binary```.  This removes the need for the Payload Enum union, which saves parsing branches that were done later on in ```command.rs```.  ```event_type``` is also removed from EventData and added directly into the HashMap during the builder phase.
- handle custom_metadata with just ```Bytes``` because evenstore does not concern itself with the serialization format of the custom metadata.  This saves multiple match branches (into_inner() during conversion to grpc model) as well as simplifies the code.

## RecordedEvent (api change and version bump)
- remove the parsing of the metadata HashMap into ```RecordedEvent.is_json``` and ```RecordedEvent.event_type``` in ```command.rs```
- added ```pub fn is_json(&self)``` and ```pub fn event_data(&self)``` to RecordedEvent.
- This might be better because the two fields get yanked from the HashMap and converted to struct fields, but the ```RecordedEvent.metadata``` is still available(but empty).   Converting to functions allows the fields to be queried lazily and leaves the metadata intact, giving it a purpose to remain inside RecordedEvent (for future extensibility).  Event Type is now also a reference to the HashMap entry for performance.  The caller can decide if they want to clone/to_owned/to_string.  In my use case, I always use json event payloads, so checking is_json isn't needed.  

I was unable to run the integration tests without failure (the doc-tests fails to compile with serde Serialize).  Everything else looks ok.

### Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Enhancement
- [ ] New feature

### Description of the changes
humanize_number has the capability to error out with very large values, in some cases over 10 quintillion (9,999,999,999,999,999,999,999), in other locales over 1,000 quintillion (9,999,999,999,999,999,999,999,999). 

This PR:
Closes #4619 and fixes the instance of this in cleanup that started this PR (prompts the user to provide a more sane number value)
Addresses this issue in audioset jukebox (prompts the user to provide a more sane number value)
Addresses this issue in trivia's payout (caps payout at 2 ** 63 - 1)
Changes the [p]roll max value to 2 ** 63 - 1 to help standardize max value across the bot
Adds to humanize_number's docstring to explain the possible limit on some systems
These should be all the places in Red where this number value for a limit could be enforced/used.

This PR does not:
Add a possible limit for triviaset payout (it's an uncapped float at the moment)
Cap anything that's passed to humanize_number via the function itself

Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ simplecov (0.20.0 → 0.21.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov) · [Changelog](https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Release Notes

0.21.2

Bugfixes

  • maximum_coverage_drop won't fail any more if .last_run.json is still in the old format. Thanks @petertellgren
  • maximum_coverage_drop won't fail if an expectation is specified for a previous unrecorded criterion, it will just pass (there's nothing, so nothing to drop)
  • fixed bug in maximum_coverage_drop calculation that could falsely report it had dropped for minimal differences

0.21.1

Bugfixes

  • minimum_coverage_by_file works again as expected (errored out before 😱)

0.21.0

The "Collate++" release making it more viable for big CI setups by limiting memory consumption. Also includes some nice new additions for branch coverage settings.

Enhancements

  • Performance of SimpleCov.collate improved - it should both run faster and consume much less memory esp. when run with many files (memory consumption should not increase with number of files any more)
  • Can now define the minimum_coverage_by_file, maximum_coverage_drop and refuse_coverage_drop by branch as well as line coverage. Thanks to @jemmaissroff
  • Can set primary coverage to something other than line by setting primary_coverage :branch in SimpleCov Configuration. Thanks to @jemmaissroff

Misc

  • reduce gem size by splitting Changelog into Changelog.md and a pre 0.18 Changelog.old.md, the latter of which is not included in the gem
  • The interface of ResultMeger.merge_and_store is changed to support the collate performance improvements mentioned above. It's not considered an official API, hence this is not in the breaking section. For people using it to merge results from different machines, it's recommended to migrate to collate.

Does any of this look wrong? Please let us know.

Commits

See the full diff on Github. The new version differs by 28 commits:

  • prep 0.21.2 release
  • More exit code check specs
  • More thorough maximum coverage drop specs + fixes
  • reformat and reformulate some cukes

  • Release prep for 0.21.0 (#963)
  • Enable and fix new cops
  • Upgrade rubocop and fix offenses
  • highlight why we can do result.to_hash.first
  • Make collate able to ignore timeouts or not
  • Only synchronize resultset around read not whole result creation
  • Explicitly make collate ignore the merge timeout
  • Restructure specs
  • Improve performance of collate & reduce memorty consumption
  • minor gem updates (#961)
  • Allows switching primary coverage to something other than line (#959)
  • Use release Ruby 3
  • Update Gemfile & JRubify them
  • Update dummy Rails application to 6.1
  • Add WEBrick to development dependencies
  • Test against latest Ruby versions
  • Extend setup instructions in Contributing
  • Fix Rubocop
  • Revert "Maybe solve PR commits not running Actions"
  • Implement branch coverage support for exit status modifiers (#934)

Bundler only enforces that version used to `bundle install` match the major version specified in the `Gemfile.lock`. We now parse the version specified in the `Gemfile.lock` and request any version of bundler that matches that major version.

author: joelddiaz
body:
s3:ListMultipartUploadParts is needed to be able to check on status of uploads. The permission is implied when the IAM user/credentials that created the MultiPartUploads is the same as the user/credentials trying to list them (see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/mpuAndPermissions.html ).

When users/credentials are rotated, there can be a disconnect between the user/creds performing the ListMultipartUploadParts and the user/creds performing the uploads.

Stop depending on the ListMultipartUploadParts permission being implicitly granted, and just explicitly list this permission as required to allow credentials rotation without a risk of losing the ability to s3:ListMultipartuploadParts.

author: dzucconi
body:
Closes: [FX-2591](https://artsyproduct.atlassian.net/browse/FX-2591)

I noticed this bug this morning when trying to use the mobile site. The go button (which in mobile Safari simulates `<enter>`) clears the input without searching.

![](https://static.damonzucconi.com/_capture/Y7M1R0p4yOvA.gif)

This was introduced here as a feature not a bug: https://github.com/artsy/reaction/pull/3217

I think it makes sense not to clear the input because frequently one wants to edit the query to refine it — this is a pretty common pattern in most searches/search engines. I couldn't find any specific accessibility guidelines on this particular point, but it makes an intuitive kind of sense. So this PR just disables the clearing of the input, rather than fixing the submission with the addition of the input clear.

We also already populate the query when linking to search results directly, anyway.

author: mabruzzo
body:
## Summary

This Pull Request makes introduces 3 key changes to the VL+CT integrator.

1. Magnetic fields can now be switched off.
    - A new `mhd_choice` parameter has been added for the VL+CT integrator to indicate whether Bfields should be included. This parameter has no default value - an error will be raised if it isn't specified.
    - To actually make this change, we refactored the `EnzoConstrainedTransport` class. The class now completely encapsulates handling of the interface bfields.
        - I'm not sold on the current design of `EnzoConstrainedTransport`.
        - Currently the class encapsulate the interface bfield and has mutable state; we need to initialize a new instance each time we call `EnzoMethodMHDVlct::compute`. I think a better design would separate the actual constrained transport operations and the responsibility of tracking the extra data used in these operations to separate classes.
        - If we ever add support for other MHD update approaches (e.g. divergence cleaning or other constrained transport methods), we'll probably want to make `EnzoConstrainedTransport` a subclass of some `EnzoBfieldUpdate` class to allow for easy swapping. Along those lines, it might also make sense to introduce a dummy Bfield updator class that is used when we don't want any bfields.
        - For now, I'm inclined to stick current design of `EnzoConstrainedTransport` and wait until a better design becomes apparent or necessary. However, if anybody has better ideas, do let me know.
    - I modified some tests that were previously used with magnetic fields set
      to 0 to now test the integrator without any magnetic fields at all.

2. Transitioned `EnzoMethodMHDVlct`, `EnzoEquationOfState`, `EnzoRiemann`, `EnzoReconstructor`, `EnzoIntegrableUpdate`, and `EnzoConstrainedTransport` away from using `Grouping`s of fields to directly employing maps/dictionaries that hold `EFlt3DArray`s. This transition affords a number of benefits:
   - This transition affords a number of benefits:
       - It simplifies the code. Our usage of `Grouping`s was already conceptually similar to a mapping, but it has an extra level of indirection.
       - It decouples the hydro algorithms from the Cello machinery.
       - Operations can be expressed more concisely. Our prior implementation exercised `Grouping`s in a manner that probably wasn't initially anticipated and likely resulted in more verbose code.
       - See the **Future Work** heading for a list of future improvements that I plan to pursue by leveraging this newer functionality
   - To help facilitate this transition we introduced the `EnzoEFlt3DArray` class which serves as a map of `EFlt3DArray`s. The implementation is fairly naive and unoptimized. I discuss potential improvements below under the **Future Work** heading.
   - This transition allowed me to drastically reduce the number of methods of `EnzoFieldArrayFactory.` In the process I was able to removed the deprecated method mentioned by Issue #69. At this point only a single non-constructor method `EnzoFieldArrayFactory::from_name`. This method builds an array that wraps a given Cello field. A future PR should probably move this functionallity to Cello's `Field` class and remove `EnzoFieldArrayFactory` completely

3. Shifted from pre-registerring the passively advected scalars in `EnzoRiemann`, `EnzoReconstructor`, `EnzoIntegrableUpdate`, and `EnzoEquationOfState` to specifying them when executing their functionallity
   - It was not originally my intention to include this change in this PR, but it kind of sneaked into it.
   - This has always been the better approach to allow for advection of passive scalars that are only registered by `Method` objects after the `EnzoMethodMHDVlct` is initialized or by subclasses of `Initial`. The (pending) introduction of the required field machinery makes this all the more important.
   - To help facilitate this change, we introduced the `EnzoNestedPassiveScalarFieldList` class to generate and cache the list of passively advected scalars. While introducing a new class to handle this isn't strictly necessary, this is a general challenge faced by all (M)HD integrators.
   - To dynamically specify specify the passively advected scalars to the integration components, we now commonly pass around a `passive_lists` argument.
       - This is initialized by `EnzoNestedPassiveScalarFieldList`.
       - It's a vector of vectors of passive scalar names (they serve as keys for the maps of arrays). The first list holds the name of all passively advected scalars that are normally advected (e.g. enzo colours). All subsequent lists hold collections of passively advected scalars whose mass fraction must sum to 1 (e.g. enzo species). There may be a better format for conveying this information, but this seemed like a reasonable way to start.
       - *Note:* A future PR still needs to add support to `EnzoMethodMHDVlct` for advecting collections of passive scalars, like species, whose mass fractions must sum to 1.
   - I also found it necessary to change `EnzoMethodMHDVlct` so that it refreshes all fields (because all fields holding passively advected scalars are not known at compile time)


Apologies about how wide reaching these changes are. It was initially my intention to just perform changes 1 and 2 (because they both will require moderate changes to the documentation). If I had been more careful, the last change could have been introduced as a separate PR, but some of the changes definitely eased the transition.

## Future Work

I just wanted to briefly mention some future changes I anticipate making thanks to this transition from `Grouping`s to `Map`s:

- I'm going to attempt to refactor `EnzoComputePressure` (and the relevant machinery in `EnzoMethodGrackle`) to make use of the `EnzoEFltArrayMap` machinery. I think this should be relatively easy to do while maintaining an interface that falls back to using the Cello fields. If successful, this will facilitate adding full Grackle support to `EnzoEquationOfState` and `EnzoMethodMHDVlct`
- It's my intention to introduce some kind of memory pool so that we don't have to allocate and deallocated memory every time we execute `EnzoMethodMHDVlct::compute`. An old benchmark I ran indicates that this should give a considerable boost in performance.
- I'm interested in playing around with the implementation in `EnzoEFltMap` to try to allow better optimization of the Riemann solvers. One could imagine adding an extra level of indirection into `EnzoEFltMap` and storing the entries in an instance of `Cello<enzo_float,4>` (with the ordering of quantities optimized for the Riemann solver).

* Fetching in batch some key properties that usually spans multiple queries
* Avoid fetching realms and user permissions in the `whoami` endpoint, but for a single and the current realm being managed from the admin console
* Avoid querying all realms from the admin console whenever possible
* When querying realms from admin console, return only the basic information

Expected results:

* Time to migrate should be reduced. If compared with the latest release, migration from a previous database takes forever. You should be able to migrate in less than 5 minutes. Depends on the database. The next step is to run using a production-grade DB. This is not a final solution though, but it helps a lot.
* Time to load the admin console is reduced. If compared with the latest release, the console just doesn't open. You should be able to open the admin console in a few seconds.

Next steps:

* The work done to the admin console should pave the road to other improvements to make the console more multi-realm friendly. We need to resume discussions on how we want to change it so that we avoid listing all realms, provide ways to search for realms, etc.
* Test using more realms (5k)

author: dreamescaper
body:
Contributes to #157.

This PR allows you to have Page (e.g. ContentPage, TabbedPage...) root element as navigation target (currently you need to have ContentView).

It was resolved in a bit hacky way.
- Added fake RootContainerHandler to use it as a root for renderer. It allows to retrieve rendered ContentPage native element.
- XF.RouteFactory's GetOrCreate method is sync, and that doesn't allow to use async rendering inside. As a workaround, I've added async method CreateAsync to MbbRouteFactory, which is called _before_ Shell navigation invoked, and GetOrCreate method simply returns already created element.
- Previously ShellNavigationManager created separate MobileBlazorBindingsRenderer on each navigation. I'm not sure that's OK, so I registered MobileBlazorBindingsRenderer as a singletone. Let me know if you have any concerns.

See detailed discussion here:
https://github.com/xamarin/MobileBlazorBindings/issues/157#issuecomment-750587312


Note that this is a breaking change, you won't be able to use ContentView as navigation target root anymore.
We can add a workaround to preserve backward compatibility (wrap non-Page result in ContentPage), but I'm not sure if we should.

Fixes #298

author: myk002
body:
Allows Label text to scroll with Up/Down/PgUp/PgDown keys, just like the ListBox classes.

Not being able to scroll Label text became an issue for quickfort because blueprint help text is displayed in a MessageBox (which uses a Label to display the text). Blueprint help text is user-defined, so long blueprint walkthroughs (I'm looking at you, dreamfort) could not be fully displayed.

I would have loved to accept Space as equivalent to PageDown, but that interacts poorly with text input fields (depending on the order components' onInput() functions are called, it could end up scrolling every time you typed a space into a text field)

author: rgrove
body:
PR #7310 introduced a regression that causes skipped SSR queries to always set `loading` to `true`, which doesn't match the behavior of `useQuery()` on the client and can result in hydration mismatches.

The problem is that `skip: true` was being treated as equivalent to `ssr: false`, but they're not actually equivalent. I think the correct solution is to let `this.getQueryResult()` provide a suitable result when `skip` is truthy, which ensures that skipped SSR queries will get the same result as skipped non-SSR queries.

An alternative approach would be to simply back out the changes from PR #7310, but then we'd lose the benefit of avoiding the unnecessary `QueryPromise` when `skip` is truthy.

Fixes #7380 (note that this issue's title and description are inaccurate, but its comments describe the problem correctly)

author: rafiss
body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #58671.

/cc @cockroachdb/release

---

The authn code needs to query system.users and system.role_options.
These queries are run by the internal executor, which has a current DB
of "". This causes the name to be resolved as "".system.users and
"".system.role_options. The lookup for the "" DB always fails, but that
result is not cached, so the lookup occurs on every authn attempt. There
is fallback logic that then looks up the correct name.

Now we specify the fully-qualified 3-part name for these two queries.

This is a low-risk change that can be backported. A more robust fix that
will prevent this class of mistaken lookups will follow later, but probably
can't be backported.

Release note (bug fix): The user authentication flow no longer performs
extraneous name lookups. This performance regression was present since
v20.2.

author: putnam3145
body:
<!-- Write **BELOW** The Headers and **ABOVE** The comments else it may not be viewable. -->
<!-- You can view Contributing.MD for a detailed description of the pull request process. -->

## About The Pull Request

Replaces single-winner score system with weird runoffs and bizarre results with one that has a much cleaner score that's easier to understand. Basically, majority judgement takes the one with the highest median and, as a tiebreaker, keeps removing median entries until one has a higher median. This leads to a weird score based on runoffs that's not very nice to look at. Usual judgment instead just counts the % of votes below the median (q) and the % above the median (p) and adds (1/2)((p-q)/(1-p-q)) to it, which leads to a reasonably understandable tiebreaker score (e.g. if the medians are 3, then the winner might have a score of 3.4 cause it has way more proponents than opponents).

## Why It's Good For The Game

Majority judgment was kinda inconsistent and results made no sense. Usual judgement has better properties and makes more sense. I kinda want to use it for maps votes, though approval is actually a degenerate case of usual judgment with only two scoring options ("yes" or "no")

## Changelog
:cl:
tweak: Replaces majority judgement with usual judgement.
/:cl:

body:
`CComBSTR(_In_opt_z_ LPCOLESTR pSrc)` calls `SysAllocString(pSrc)` which doesn't append the null-terminator
`CComBSTR(_In_ int nSize, _In_reads_opt_(nSize) LPCOLESTR sz)` calls `SysAllocStringLen(sz, nSize)` which does append the null-terminator.
